corpus.comment: Provenance for every count in this file. The original four hosts and three package grants came from ONE measured install pass; the rest come from reading 230 published packages' actual source. Both bases are legitimate and the per-entry `evidence` field says which one an entry rests on. The denominators live here so a reader can check any percentage below rather than take it on faith.
corpus.method: `npm pack` the published tarball, follow the require chain, resolve LITERAL hostnames to a file:line, decide the filesystem axis, classify the failure on denial. Never installed, never executed.
corpus.whyTheProjectFsNumbersDiffer: 67 packages recorded `read` or `readwrite` on the project axis, which reads as 67 carve-out candidates and is NOT what it means. 31 of them touch only paths under their OWN package directory (`./build/Release`, `./prebuilds/`, `./vendor/`), which the jail's baseline `package_dir` rw already grants; of the 36 that genuinely reach the consumer project, most read only `<project>/package.json` or walk up through `node_modules` — both already granted read by `grant_build_jail_dependency_reads`. The residue needing a NEW grant is the git-hook cohort plus two project-file writers, which is what `packageGrants` below carries. The 67 figure is the honest measurement; eleven new grants is the honest consequence.

failureModeCounts.comment: After normalizing the lanes' free-text `failure_mode` strings onto the enum (the map is in `failureModes.normalization`). Normalizing MOVED THE HEADLINE: 31 entries were the literal string `SILENT`, but three more encoded a silent primary in prose, so the real primary-SILENT count is 34, and 36 packages have a silent component somewhere.

corpus.threatModel: What the jail is FOR, which decides how to read every count below. The attack it blunts is the Shai-Hulud shape: an attacker publishes a new preinstall or postinstall into a package that never had one, and it runs with the user's complete access. The defense is PACKAGE IDENTITY — a package with no entry in this catalog gets nothing, and a package that needs network or filesystem access arrives through a PULL REQUEST here first. That makes the whole surface opt-in. It also means host granularity is worth much less than it looks: narrowing an admitted host constrains a package somebody already reviewed, and does nothing about the unvetted package a worm just reached. Granting a listed package the ability to fetch arbitrary code is a known, accepted fact.

networkHosts.artifact: Node headers and libs for a from-source native compile
networkHosts.observed: node-gyp's `lib/process-release.js:75` `distBaseUrl = 'https://nodejs.org/dist'`, the default reached whenever the header cache at `~/.cache/node-gyp/<ver>` is cold. 81 of the 230 source-read packages can reach it — 55% of every network-needing package and the largest single cohort by a wide margin. TWO limits on that number, stated because they cut in opposite directions. It UNDERSTATES the mechanism: `fetchedBy` is the corpus subset, not the ecosystem, and any package with a `binding.gyp` joins the cohort. It OVERSTATES the common path: for most of the 81 the fetch is a FALLBACK — a bundled or downloaded prebuild is tried first, and nub sets `npm_config_nodedir` to the provisioned Node root, so node-gyp finds local headers and never leaves the machine. The entry is what keeps the fallback from being a hard failure, not what a normal install exercises. NOT observed in the earlier 311-package corpus run for exactly that reason; absence there is evidence the harness had warm headers, not that the entry is unnecessary.

Named in Prisma's own firewall-allowlist documentation. A grep of the fetched postinstall bundle found no literal match, so the constant lives in a helper chunk that pass did not fetch. Not independently confirmed from source, and `@prisma/engines` is not in the 230-package source-read corpus, so v2 adds nothing to this entry.

Resolved by cypress's postinstall in the corpus harness-validation run. Paired with cdn.cypress.io because the 302 lands there; granting only one leaves the install broken. Corroborated by v2's source read of cypress@15.19.0, which also found the binary is unzipped into a per-user cache OUTSIDE the project (`cachedir('Cypress')`), not into the package dir.

Resolved by cypress's postinstall in the corpus harness-validation run, as the redirect target of download.cypress.io. cypress is the one corpus package that installs successfully under v1's four-host list.

networkHosts.artifact: Prebuilt native binaries and vendor CLIs published as GitHub Release assets; CLDR data as repository archives
networkHosts.observed: The `prebuild-install` / `@mapbox/node-pre-gyp` GitHub-Releases default, and the single largest gap in v1. `prebuild-install/util.js:57` `urlTemplate()` falls back to `github(opts.pkg) + '/releases/download/{tag_prefix}{version}/' + packageName` whenever a package sets no `binary.host` (canvas is the reference case: its `binary` block carries only `napi_versions`). node-pre-gyp reaches the same default through `lib/util/versioning.js:317`. 40 of the 230 packages resolve a github.com URL; with nodejs.org that is 115 of 146 network-needing packages (79%). Every observed use is a plain GET under one of the two path shapes above — never a bare repository, never an API route. ONE corpus package escapes that shape and it is called out in `notGranted.deferred`: node-libcurl `git clone`s `github.com/microsoft/vcpkg.git` on its Windows source-build fallback, which is whole-repo access AND a gateway to vcpkg's own port-source hosts, a set that is not enumerable. `zeromq` names github.com only through cmake-ts/vcpkg on a path the source read established is NOT taken on the common path, so its membership in this list is conservative. `install-artifact-from-github` is a shared helper rather than a leaf dependency — it is listed because it is the mechanism re2 and others reach the host THROUGH, and because it honours a GITHUB_SERVER_URL / per-package `*_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR` override that a user can point elsewhere.
networkHosts.residual: github.com serves `git-receive-pack` — an authenticated WRITE — on the same hostname. RATIFIED: the host is admitted. What bounds the residual is the jail itself, not the host: `defaults::lifecycle_scrubbed_env` withholds the whole credential family (registry auth, any key containing TOKEN / SECRET / AUTH), and `~/.ssh`, `~/.git-credentials`, `.npmrc` and `<project>/.git` are ungranted, so a confined script has no push credential and an unauthenticated push is rejected. Bounded further by package identity: only a package with a catalog entry reaches it at all.

networkHosts.artifact: GitHub Releases metadata, used to build a better error message on a failed asset download
networkHosts.observed: @cubejs-backend/cubestore queries the Releases API only AFTER its asset download has already failed, to name the available assets in the error it then throws; it does not retry the download from the response. The host is therefore not load-bearing for a successful install — it is admitted so the failure a user sees is the real one rather than a DNS error masking it.
networkHosts.residual: The REST API is write-capable across the board, and a token is what makes it so. RATIFIED; bounded by the same env scrub as github.com and by package identity.

networkHosts.artifact: npm packages fetched by a lifecycle script that shells its own `npm install`, or reads a tarball off the registry directly
networkHosts.observed: Six packages reach the registry from inside their own lifecycle script rather than through the installer. `node`'s postinstall (node-bin-setup@1.1.4 `index.js`) spawns `npm install --no-save <prefix>-<platform>-<arch>@<version>` to fetch the real per-arch Node distribution AS A REGISTRY PACKAGE. `@netlify/esbuild` shells `npm install` and, on failure, falls back to a raw `https.get('https://registry.npmjs.org/' + pkg + '/-/' + … + '.tgz')` and hand-parses the tar. `exifreader` reaches it transitively through an `npx -p …` invocation. `install-peers` installs the consumer's peerDependencies for real — and is refused on the filesystem axis (see notGranted.packages), so this host does not rescue it.
networkHosts.residual: `npm publish` is a PUT to the host that serves the read. RATIFIED. Bounded by the same env scrub — the registry-auth family is withheld and `.npmrc` sits inside the secret-file read deny floor, so a confined script holds no publish credential — and by package identity.

networkHosts.artifact: Vendored binaries and data files served straight out of a repository tree
networkHosts.observed: The imagemin `*-bin` family builds its BinWrapper source URLs from this host: `pngquant-bin/lib/index.js:6` sets `url` to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imagemin/pngquant-bin/v${version}/vendor/` with per-OS suffixes, and jpegtran-bin is the same line against its own repo. free-email-domains fetches two disposable-domain blocklists from it. Read-only by construction — raw.githubusercontent.com serves repository content and accepts nothing.

networkHosts.artifact: The same vendored binaries, via the legacy hostname alias
networkHosts.observed: A SEPARATE entry rather than a note on raw.githubusercontent.com, because four packages hardcode the legacy alias literally — zopflipng-bin's `lib/index.js`, and gif2webp-bin / jpeg-recompress-bin at `lib/index.js:7` — and the allowlist gates the name the client resolves, not the name it eventually redirects to. Granting only the modern host leaves these four broken at DNS. Same read-only property.

networkHosts.artifact: Chrome / Chromium / chromedriver builds from Google-operated buckets
networkHosts.observed: puppeteer's default, through `@puppeteer/browsers@3.0.6 lib/browser-data/chrome.js:26` `resolveDownloadUrl(platform, buildId, baseUrl='https://storage.googleapis.com/chrome-for-testing-public')`. @sitespeed.io/chromedriver builds the same prefix at `install.js:47`. @percy/core reaches `/chromium-browser-snapshots/` only when `PERCY_CHROMIUM_BASE_URL` is explicitly set, so it is opt-in and not on the default path. puppeteer alone justifies the entry.
networkHosts.residual: The bucket is in the PATH, not the hostname, so this is a genuinely multi-tenant name: an attacker can rent a bucket. RATIFIED and accepted as a known residual — puppeteer is the package, and a broken puppeteer is the worse outcome. Bounded by package identity. Contrast the bucket-scoped names admitted elsewhere (`hummus.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com`, the CloudFront distributions): there the tenant IS the hostname, so an exact-host rule already pins one tenant and no residual exists.

networkHosts.observed: `chrome.js:45` `baseVersionUrl`, reached by `resolveBuildId()` only when the configured buildId is a channel name or milestone ('latest', 'stable') rather than the concrete pinned id `PUPPETEER_REVISIONS` supplies by default. Conditional, and admitted so a consumer who pins a channel is not broken. A GitHub Pages host: static content, accepts nothing.

networkHosts.artifact: Prebuilt gRPC native extension and protoc/grpc_node_plugin binaries
networkHosts.observed: Both set an explicit `binary.host` — grpc's block is `{module_name:'grpc_node', host:'https://node-precompiled-binaries.grpc.io/', remote_path:'{name}/v{version}', …}` — which `@mapbox/node-pre-gyp/lib/util/versioning.js:317` prefers over the github.com default. A dedicated single-tenant vendor host, so this is a strictly narrower grant than the github.com one it displaces, and a correction to an inferred claim that had both packages down as github.com fetchers.

`download.js`: `const cdn = options.cdnUrl || process.env.NGROK_CDN_URL || 'https://bin.equinox.io'`. @shopify/ngrok's copy was diffed against standalone ngrok's and is near byte-identical — same default host, same `/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-` path, same per-platform archive map. Equinox is a binary-distribution service; the path carries an opaque per-vendor channel id.

`package.json` `binary.host = 'https://npm.duckdb.org/duckdb'`, taken by node-pre-gyp's `versioning.js:317` in preference to any GitHub-Releases default. Recorded explicitly because the inferred claim had duckdb down as a github.com fetcher and the source read shows it is NOT — a dedicated vendor host instead. grpc-tools and hummus carry the same correction.

@sitespeed.io/edgedriver's `install.js` `getDriverUrl()` builds `const base = process.env.EDGEDRIVER_BASE_URL || 'https://msedgedriver.microsoft.com/<version>/'`. edgedriver's `dist/constants.js` sets the same value as `BASE_CDN_URL`. A dedicated vendor download host, not a shared user-content CDN.

`dist/install.js` `downloadDriver()`'s catch block falls back to `EDGEDRIVER_BUCKET = 'https://msedgewebdriverstorage.blob.core.windows.net/edgewebdriver?…'`. Admitted alongside the primary because a fallback that resolves nowhere converts a recoverable failure into a hard one. A per-storage-account hostname, so the tenant is the name.

`EDGE_PRODUCTS_API = 'https://edgeupdates.microsoft.com/api/products'` is DECLARED in edgedriver's bundle but was not observed being called from the install path. Admitted rather than left out: the constant is real, the cost of the entry is one hostname, and the alternative is a version-resolution path that silently fails on some future release.

`lib/updater.js` requires Node's BUILT-IN `https` module — which is why the inferred claim missed this host entirely, reasoning from tldjs having no HTTP-client dependency — and reads the URL from tldjs's own `package.json` field `tldjs.providers['publicsuffix-org']`. A static publication site.

networkHosts.artifact: A hosted CSV of free email domains
networkHosts.observed: One of three entries in `scripts/postinstall.mjs`'s SOURCES array, fetched with global `fetch()`; there is no override env var, so the host is not avoidable. A HubSpot file-hosting CDN — read-only; HubSpot writes go through api.hubapi.com, a different hostname.

`package.json` `binary.host = 'https://hummus.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com'` with `remote_path = './{module_name}/v{version}/{toolset}/'` — an S3 bucket, not GitHub Releases, and another correction to an inferred github.com claim. The bucket name IS the hostname (virtual-hosted style), so an exact-host rule pins exactly one tenant.

`package.json` `binary.host = 'https://axonodegit.s3.amazonaws.com/nodegit/nodegit/'`, consumed by node-pre-gyp's default URL template from `lifecycleScripts/install.js`'s `spawn('node-pre-gyp', ['install', '--fallback-to-build'])`. Bucket-as-hostname, single tenant.
`scripts/build_dependencies/build_step_tar.js:44` sets the host literally. A CloudFront distribution id is per-distribution, so the hostname is the tenant.

`scripts/extension/support/constants.js` declares `MIRRORS = ['https://d135dj0rjqvssy.cloudfront.net', 'https://appsignal-agent-releases.global.ssl.fastly.net']`, with the per-platform filename AND its checksum pinned in the same bundled file (the TRIPLES map). Both mirrors are admitted because the package walks the list.
The second entry of the same MIRRORS array. A per-service Fastly hostname; the artifact is checksum-pinned by the package itself.
`install.js`: `const binariesSource = process.env.TON_CLIENT_BIN_SRC || 'https://binaries.tonlabs.io'`, then a raw `http`/`https.get` piped through `zlib` gunzip. Dedicated single-tenant vendor host.

networkHosts.artifact: Azure Stream Analytics local-run service package
networkHosts.observed: `lib/install.js` `downloadZip()` reads the bundled `docs/downloadfilelist_settings.json` and GETs the entry's `fileUrl`, which resolves to exactly `https://usqldownload.blob.core.windows.net/ext/asa/ASALocalRunService.1.4.0-dotnet.core.8.x.zip`. Per-storage-account hostname.

`lib/binary.js`: `const BINARY_LOCATION = 'https://package.cli.amplify.aws'`; also observed in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run as `getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN package.cli.amplify.aws`, followed by `failed to install amplify binary`. v1 REFUSED this as `not-blocking` because the install still exits 0. v2 admits it, and the reversal is the point: exit 0 with the binary missing is precisely the SILENT class — the CLI is broken at first use, on a green install. @aws-amplify/cli's normalized failure mode is SILENT. 'Not blocking' was the wrong test.

networkHosts.artifact: librdkafka's Windows dependencies, as NuGet packages
networkHosts.observed: `binding.gyp`'s `OS=='win'` conditional action runs `python deps/windows-install.py`, whose `downloadBaseUrl` is `env['NODE_RDKAFKA_NUGET_BASE_URL'] || 'https://globalcdn.nuget.org/packages/'`. Windows-only in practice; see `windowsNetworkNote`.

networkHosts.artifact: The Visual Studio Build Tools installer
networkHosts.observed: A hardcoded `installerUrl` for `vs_BuildTools.exe` in windows-build-tools' `dist/constants.js`. Admitted as a single-tenant Microsoft download host. NOTE what the package then DOES with it — it runs the downloaded installer, a system-wide elevated change; that is a filesystem and exec concern the jail handles on its own axes, and refusing the hostname would not have prevented it.

networkHosts.artifact: The Visual C++ Build Tools installer
networkHosts.observed: The second hardcoded installer URL in the same file, for `visualcppbuildtools_full.exe`.

`dist/constants.js`: `pythonMirror = inGFW.osSync() ? 'https://npm.taobao.org/mirrors/python' : 'https://www.python.org/ftp/python'`. The python.org arm is the default everywhere the `in-gfw` heuristic does not fire; the taobao mirror is refused separately as a retired host.

networkHosts.artifact: Chromium snapshot builds, through the Cloud Storage JSON API
networkHosts.observed: chromium's bundled `config.js` sets `CDN_URL` to this host rather than to storage.googleapis.com. ADMITTED ON RE-EXAMINATION (v3): v2 refused it as `write-capable`, which was the over-tight reasoning the best-effort thesis rejects — chromium's failure mode is SILENT, so refusing it produced a green install with no browser and a user who finds out at first use. A broken package is the outcome to avoid; a residual is not. `NODE_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD_HOST` remains a documented override.
networkHosts.residual: The broadest hostname in the set: www.googleapis.com fronts essentially every Google API, authenticated write and upload routes included. Bounded the same way as every other residual here — the lifecycle env scrub withholds the credential family, so a confined script holds no token for any of those routes — and bounded further by package identity: `chromium` is the only package with an entry naming it.

networkHosts.artifact: Sauce Connect tunnel binary and its version index
networkHosts.observed: `SAUCE_API_HOST` defaults to 'saucelabs.com' and is used for /versions.json and the download. ADMITTED ON RE-EXAMINATION (v3): v2 refused it because the bare apex also serves an authenticated web application, which is exactly the reasoning the best-effort thesis drops. The download is opt-in (behind an explicit env var) and a no-op by default, so the refusal only bit the user who ASKED for the tunnel — and broke them. `SAUCE_API_HOST` remains overridable.
networkHosts.residual: An apex domain that also serves an interactive credentialed web app, so the artifact path and a login surface share one hostname with no subdomain between them. Bounded by the env scrub and by package identity.

windowsNetworkNote: Seven entries above carry `"platform": "win32"`, and under the CURRENT Windows posture none of them can be reached: `preset::build_jail_net` compiles to `false` — deny-all — on Windows, because the backend refuses a per-host policy outright (`WinNetPlan::PerHostUnsupported`; the available AppContainer exemption exposes every loopback listener, so a local forwarder would bypass the hostname gate). The entries are recorded anyway. They are the evidence a Windows per-host gate would be written against, and an entry that exists before the capability does is what stops the capability from shipping with a guessed allowlist.

packageNetwork.comment: PER-PACKAGE EGRESS, and the axis that carries the build jail's actual security argument. THE DEFENSE IS PACKAGE IDENTITY, NOT HOST GRANULARITY. The attack this jail exists to blunt is the Shai-Hulud shape: an attacker publishes a new postinstall into a package that never had one, and it runs with the user's full access. That package is not one anybody vetted — it is whatever the worm reached. So the control that matters is the ENTRY: a package with no entry gets no egress, whatever hosts it wants, and a package that needs egress arrives through a PULL REQUEST against this file. That PR is the whole opt-in mechanism, and it is the sentence that explains why this catalog exists.
packageNetwork.hostLists: NOT AUTHORED HERE. build.rs INVERTS `networkHosts[].fetchedBy`, which already records per host which packages fetch it, into a per-package map. Restating the same facts package-first would be two sources that drift.
packageNetwork.fullSupersedes: A `full` entry replaces any inverted host list for that package rather than adding to it — node-libcurl legitimately appears under both github.com and nodejs.org, and a merged view would claim a precision the grant does not have.
packageNetwork.enforcementStatus: NOT YET ENFORCED — READ THIS BEFORE RELYING ON THE MODEL ABOVE. `preset::build_jail_net` compiles to `["$downloads"]` for EVERY jailed lifecycle spawn, and `compile_build_jail`'s `package_name` reaches only the filesystem axis. So today a package with NO entry still reaches all 33 admitted hosts, and the package-identity gate described here is data without an enforcer. Generated as PACKAGE_NETWORK_FULL / PACKAGE_NETWORK_HOSTS and exposed as `compiler::package_network()` so the compiler can consume it. Closing the gap is the highest-value change this catalog now makes possible and is tracked as `knownDefects: per-package-egress-not-enforced`.

reasons.unenumerable: the package reaches a transitive host set nothing enumerates
reasons.undetermined: the host could not be resolved to a literal from the published source
reasons.runtime-selected: the host is chosen at run time, so no static list can be correct

full.why: The case that motivated this axis. Its Windows source-build fallback git-clones github.com/microsoft/vcpkg.git — whole-repository, not one asset — and then, once vcpkg installs the curl, openssl, zlib and libssh2 ports, reaches vcpkg's OWN per-port download hosts. That set is plural, per-port, and not derivable from node-libcurl's manifest, so no host list can be right. Full egress for this one package is the honest grant.
full.observed: binary.host for the prebuilt path plus, on the source-build fallback, the vcpkg clone and its transitive port fetches, read from the published tarball. Previously recorded in notGranted.deferred as the case a path-scoped github.com grant would break; under the package-identity model it simply gets full egress instead.
full.platform: win32 (the fallback path); the entry is unconditional because the grant cannot be platform-scoped today

full.why: Its cmake-ts/vcpkg build path was not traced to literal hosts — likely github.com/microsoft/vcpkg plus individual port sources, through cmake-ts's own dependency rather than zeromq's. The common path ships a prebuilt addon and needs nothing, so this grant is inert for most consumers and correct for the one who falls back.
full.observed: script/install.js tries lib/load-addon.js first, which resolves a shipped build/<os>/<arch>/... addon.node via build/manifest.json; only a miss reaches the cmake-ts path, which the source read recorded as undetermined.

full.why: Its host cannot be read from source because the CODE IS NOT PUBLISHED: package.json declares `postinstall: node dist/index.js` and a `files` list containing `dist`, but the published tarball contains no dist/ at all — only a placeholder `hasura` text file that says it is 'to be automatically replaced by Hasura CLI binary file by postinstall lifecycle hooks'. The download is certain, the host is unknowable from the artifact.
full.observed: The published tarball for this version contains only `hasura` (a placeholder), LICENSE, README.md and package.json. No dist/, so the postinstall entry point does not exist in what npm ships.

full.why: Downloads a real Redis server binary into a find-cache-dir location. The URL is assembled across its own compiled RedisBinaryDownloadUrl.js rather than stated as a literal, so the source read could not resolve a hostname — the mongodb-memory-server family's shape, where the mirror is configurable and version-dependent.
full.observed: postinstall calls RedisBinary.getPath({}) from lib/util/RedisBinary.js; the sibling modules RedisBinaryDownload.js and RedisBinaryDownloadUrl.js plus the find-cache-dir dependency establish the download without yielding a literal host.

full.why: Its Python mirror is chosen by a NETWORK PROBE: `pythonMirror = inGFW.osSync() ? 'https://npm.taobao.org/mirrors/python' : 'https://www.python.org/ftp/python'`, where in-gfw decides by testing reachability at run time. A static host list cannot be correct for both outcomes, and one of the two arms is a retired host that is refused. Four hosts across two installers besides.
full.observed: dist/constants.js: the in-gfw-driven pythonMirror ternary, plus hardcoded installerUrls on download.visualstudio.microsoft.com and download.microsoft.com. Note what the package then DOES — it runs the downloaded installers, a system-wide elevated change the filesystem and exec axes govern, not this one.

full.why: A shared helper (re2 and others reach GitHub Releases THROUGH it) whose host is whatever the consumer points it at: it honours GITHUB_SERVER_URL and a per-package `<NAME>_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR` override. A host list would be wrong for every user who sets either, which is the documented way to use a private mirror.
full.observed: The default is the github.com Releases pattern, overridable via GITHUB_SERVER_URL or a package-specific *_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR, read from the published tarball.

systemPaths.comment: A NEW AXIS in v2. 17 of the 230 source-read packages need SYSTEM library or header paths to build, 12 of them on the DEFAULT build path — a class the schema could not express at all, so it was silently absent from the jail rather than deliberately excluded.
systemPaths.recommendation: Grant these directories READ-ONLY, COARSELY, by default. Not a hedge — coarse is the correct answer here and the per-package alternative is worse. Three reasons. (1) The directories are world-readable and hold no secrets: /usr/lib, /usr/include, the multiarch dirs, the Homebrew prefixes, the Xcode SDK. Read access to them confers nothing a dependency could not get by shipping its own copy of a header. (2) The 17 packages do NOT cluster on an exotic mechanism — they are the ordinary native-build long tail (OpenSSL, ODBC, X11, Postgres, Kerberos, libsecret, JDK, Xcode frameworks) — which means the set is open-ended and any enumeration will be wrong for the eighteenth package. (3) Discovery is INDIRECT: pkg-config, pg_config, krb5-config and curl-config are EXECUTED during binding.gyp variable evaluation and their stdout is what supplies the include and link paths, so the paths a per-package grant would have to name are not knowable from the manifest at all. Read-only, coarse, on by default.
systemPaths.status: RECORDED, NOT YET ENFORCED. build.rs generates `SYSTEM_READ_PATHS_{LINUX,MACOS,WINDOWS}` from the arrays below and `compiler::system_read_paths()` returns the host platform's. Nothing folds them into `build_jail_surface` yet — that changes the granted read set on every platform and is a separate, measured change (tracked as `system-paths-not-enforced` in `knownDefects`). Until then this object is the recorded recommendation plus its evidence, and the 17 packages below are expected to fail.
systemPaths.envAnchored: An entry may begin with `$NAME` (POSIX) or `%NAME%` (Windows). Those are resolved by the EMBEDDER against the build environment, not by the compiler — `$JAVA_HOME` and `$SDKROOT` have no meaning to a path matcher, and hardcoding a guess for either would be wrong on most hosts.

packageGrants.mechanism: scripts/postinstall.js does three things, and each masks the next: it calls process.chdir(INIT_CWD); createDefaultGeneratedThrowFiles unconditionally mkdirs path.join(__dirname, '../../../.prisma'), a sibling of @prisma in the package's own enclosing node_modules; then it re-execs the prisma CLI as `prisma generate`, which reads the consumer's prisma/ schema directory. The generated client lands inside package_dir and needs no grant.
packageGrants.observed:
TWO MEASUREMENTS, one per platform, and the Linux one changed the code.
macOS (macos-arm64): EPERM mkdir <own node_modules>/.prisma, then EPERM uv_cwd on chdir(INIT_CWD), then EPERM reading the consumer's prisma/ schema. Verified by artifact, not exit code: a generated client of 71282 B carrying a per-run schema nonce, against absent output and 2 EPERMs without the grants.
LINUX (6.17.0-1021-gcp, Landlock ABI 7, kernel-enforced, 2026-07-29): the grant did NOT work and the blocking stage is the FIRST one. `landlock_add_rule` takes an O_PATH descriptor, so a rule for a path that does not exist cannot be attached at all — the `.prisma` grant evaporated at launch and `mkdir` was denied identically with AND without it, which is exactly the DIFFERS-either-way result that put this in knownDefects. Fixed by `curated::materialize_sibling`, which creates the directory during policy compilation; that adds no access, since the subtree is already granted rw, it only makes the access attachable. Granting the PARENT's MAKE_DIR right instead was not available: the parent is the enclosing node_modules, which holds .bin and the virtual store.
THE LINUX ARTIFACT DIFFERENTIAL, three arms on the real published 6.19.3 postinstall: UNCONFINED produced .prisma/client at 26336 B; GRANTED produced 26336 B — byte-identical to unconfined; UNGRANTED produced 0 B with `EACCES: permission denied, mkdir .../node_modules/.prisma` raised at scripts/postinstall.js:248 via createDefaultGeneratedThrowFiles (:205) from main (:67), AND EXIT CODE 0. That exit 0 over an absent artifact is this entry's SILENT failure mode, observed rather than inferred.
HONEST LIMIT ON THAT ARTIFACT: the 26336 B is the THROW-STUBS, not a generated client, in all three arms INCLUDING unconfined — so the per-run nonce does not appear anywhere and could not. On 6.19.3 the postinstall never runs `prisma generate`: getLocalPackagePath() does `require.resolve('prisma')`, which throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND because prisma 6.19.3's `main` points at build/index.js while resolution lands on build/types.js, which is not shipped; the script then warns 'please install Prisma CLI' and stops. Verified directly. The macOS observation of a 71282 B nonce-bearing client is therefore NOT reproducible on the version this entry names, and that discrepancy is recorded rather than smoothed over — see knownDefects: prisma-macos-artifact-unreproduced. The Linux conclusion does not depend on it: unconfined-equals-granted is a stronger control than artifact presence, because it pins the grant to the no-jail baseline.

A LATER CORPUS RUN MEASURED THIS PACKAGE AS A COMPLETE NO-OP EVEN UNJAILED, which contradicts that EPERM. With the grants, msw's worker script is present; without them, absent. The same later corpus run measured msw as a no-op even unjailed, and here that is CONSISTENT rather than contradictory: msw's postinstall is a no-op unless the consumer's manifest declares msw.workerDirectory, and a fixture that does not declare it exercises nothing. failureModes.comment: What a denied grant DOES to the package, recorded per package because the answer changes what a measurement can see. LOUD is the case every exit-code harness catches. SILENT is the one none of them can: a try/catch or a `|| exit 0` means the script exits 0 having skipped its real work, so the install is GREEN and the breakage surfaces later at runtime — strictly worse for a user than an install error, and structurally invisible to any measurement that reads a status code. That single fact is the strongest argument for admitting source-read as an evidence class alongside measured.

enum.LOUD: the denial fails the install with a non-zero exit and a visible error
enum.SILENT: the denial is swallowed; the install exits 0 with the package's real work not done
enum.GRACEFUL: the denial is handled and the package still ends up correct — a real fallback path, or a no-op it was always going to take
enum.UNDETERMINED: not established by the source read. A real value, not a placeholder: guessing one of the three would assert more than was read.

normalization.comment: The source-read lanes wrote free text into this field — 14 distinct values across 230 packages, one of them a 400-character paragraph. The map is keyed on the EXACT original string rather than pattern-matched, so a future lane inventing a new phrasing fails the build instead of being silently guessed at. Composite values keep BOTH modes: `primary` is what a plain denial on the default path produces, `secondary` is the other mode the entry recorded, and `note` carries the condition that selects between them. Normalizing MOVED THE HEADLINE COUNT: 31 entries were the literal string SILENT, but three more (egg-ci, react-tsparticles, ttf2woff2) encoded a silent primary in prose, so primary-SILENT is 34 and 36 packages have a silent component.

notGranted.comment: Documentation only. Nothing in this object is compiled into any allowlist. It records what a real install was measured or read to need and that was NOT admitted, so a contributor can see the bar before opening a PR. A build-time check keeps `hosts` disjoint from `networkHosts`. v2 adds `packages`, and that addition is CONCEPTUAL rather than clerical: without it every measured break reads as a carve-out candidate, and a break list has already been mischaracterized that way once. A `packages` entry means the denial is the jail WORKING — the break is expected and correct, and a PR to 'fix' it should be closed with a link here.

hosts.detail: RE-EXAMINED IN v3 AND THE VERDICT SURVIVES, ON A DIFFERENT REASON. v2 refused it because the POST body is the product, which is the over-tight security framing the best-effort thesis drops. The reason it stays refused is simply that nothing breaks: `@pact-foundation/pact-node`'s beacon is `needle.post(...).on('error', function(){})` — fire-and-forget with an explicit error handler — so a denied analytics host does not fail the install, and the source read says so directly ('a DENIED analytics-only host does not fail the install, but a denied github.com download does'). The artifact host it actually needs is github.com, which IS admitted. This is the same class of reason as npm.taobao.org: the entry would buy nothing. If a package ever NEEDS a telemetry host to function, grant it and record the residual.
hosts.observed: standalone/install.js's needle.post to /collect, with `.on('error', function(){})` attached, read from the published tarball alongside the github.com Releases download that is the real artifact fetch. PACT_DO_NOT_TRACK / config.pact_do_not_track disable it outright.

hosts.detail: Refused because an entry would grant nothing. The mirror was sunset in 2021 (superseded by registry.npmmirror.com) and no longer serves this path, so admitting the name adds an allowlist member with no reachable artifact behind it. The selection is also not user-driven: windows-build-tools picks the mirror from the `in-gfw` dependency's own network-based China-detection heuristic. The default arm, www.python.org, IS admitted, so the package is not blocked by this refusal wherever the heuristic does not fire.

Recorded as an evidenced candidate, not as a disqualification: no write-capable route or multi-tenant namespace has been established for it, and the fetch is a dedicated single-tenant vendor binary path. Retained as `undecided` through v2 because the package is absent from the 230-package source-read corpus, so nothing new bears on it. Note the requester is wrangler 1.x, which prints its own deprecation notice directing users to the `wrangler` package — so the demand may not survive the version it was measured on.
hosts.observed: Downloading release from <url>, then Error fetching release: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN workers.cloudflare.com, in the denied arm of the Linux corpus run.

packages.detail: The worst thing in the corpus. tsbl.js loops over three hardcoded competitor package names (@ngx-tour/core, ngx-ui-tour-core, @ngx-tour/ngx-popper) and requires each one's package.json; Node's resolution walks up through node_modules, so ANY of them resolving anywhere up-tree triggers `child_process.exec("rm -rf ../")` — fire-and-forget, no callback, no error handling. npm sets a lifecycle script's cwd to its own package directory, so `../` is the consumer's entire node_modules for a top-level dependency. Not a bug and not historical: it ships in the current `latest`.
packages.observed: tsbl.js:31, read from the published tarball, with the three trigger package names at the top of the same file. Independently re-verified against the current `latest` dist-tag.

A dependency's postinstall authoring the consumer's CI workflow is a write to the file that runs their pipeline; it is not a compatibility gap.
packages.observed: install.js:15 (the root computation), :98-101 (the workflow write), :112 (the LICENSE write). Read from the published tarball.

Writing another dependency's source before that source is executed is the exact vector the jail exists to close, and it is worse than the project-root writes beside it.

The postinstall is `bun ./bin/build.js install`, so it also hard-depends on the Bun runtime binary.

packages.wants: write access to five files at the consumer project root
packages.detail: scripts/install.js does five `copyFileSync('files/X', '../../X')` calls — npm sets cwd to the package's own directory, so `../../` is the consumer project root — scaffolding .webdevtoolkitrc, gulpfile.babel.js, .eslintignore, .eslintrc and stylelint.config.js. Two of those are lint config a CI gate reads and one is a build script. Contrast @cypress/snapshot, which IS granted: one file, fixed name. The line is the size and openness of the target set.
packages.observed: The five copyFileSync calls with literal relative destinations, read from the published tarball.

packages.wants: write access to the consumer project root and cypress/plugins/
packages.detail: src/add-plugin.js climbs three directories up via path.join(process.cwd(),'..','..','..') to reach the project root, then shelljs-copies plugin.js and cy-ts-preprocessor.js into cypress/plugins/ and fs.writeFileSync's tsconfig.json at the root. Gated only by an 'am I a direct dependency' heuristic, which is not consent. Overwriting the consumer's tsconfig.json from a postinstall changes how their whole project compiles.
packages.observed: The three-level climb, the shelljs copies, and the tsconfig.json write, read from the published tarball.

packages.wants: write access to the consumer's node_modules and package.json
packages.detail: Reads the consumer's package.json for peerDependencies, chdirs to INIT_CWD, and shells a REAL npm or yarn install into the consumer's node_modules; on the yarn path `yarn add --peer` also rewrites the consumer's package.json. A dependency's postinstall running the package manager is an unbounded install of packages the user never asked for, executed inside the install it is part of — a re-entrant install whose contents no lockfile describes.
packages.observed: install.js: `rootPath = process.env.INIT_CWD || …`, getPackageConfig() reading <rootPath>/package.json, then `process.chdir(rootPath)` before invoking npm or yarn.

packages.wants: write access to the consumer's .git/hooks and to `git config --local`
packages.detail: THE MOST CONTESTABLE ENTRY HERE, recorded as contestable rather than settled. Nine other git-hook installers ARE granted (see packageGrants) on the reasoning that installing hooks is what the user asked for. This one differs in two ways: it REMOVES every hook file whose name is absent from its config on every install — so it deletes hooks the user or another tool wrote, not just its own — and it runs `git config --local core.hooksPath`, redirecting where git looks for hooks at all. Deleting a sibling tool's hook is a destructive effect on state the package does not own. The cost of the refusal is real and is stated: denial is SILENT, so the user gets a green install with no hooks and finds out at their next commit. If this is reversed, the grant needs `.git/hooks` write plus a separate decision about `git config --local`, and it should be reversed deliberately rather than by someone reading the break as a bug.
packages.observed: getProjectRootDirectoryFromNodeModules() with special-cased pnpm/.deno/.store/yarn-berry walk-ups; _getHooksDirPath() shelling `execSync('git config --local core.hooksPath')`; the per-hook write loop and the paired removal of every undeclared hook name.

packages.wants: write access to a global npm-prefix bin directory
packages.detail: postinstall.js's getInstallationPath() resolves `process.env.npm_config_prefix + '/bin'` (or npm_config_prefix itself on win32), mkdirps it, and fs.renames its bundled binary there. For an ordinary local (non -g) install npm_config_prefix commonly still points at the shell's effective GLOBAL prefix, so this writes an executable into a system- or user-wide bin directory that is on PATH, outside the project entirely. A project-level dependency install reaching a shared bin dir is out of scope for a project sandbox regardless of the author's intent, and the mechanism is a hand-rolled emulation of npm's own bin linking.
packages.observed: getInstallationPath()'s npm_config_prefix derivation and verifyAndPlaceBinary()'s fs.rename into it.

packages.detail: scripts/install_completion.js: `var completionDir = '/etc/bash_completion.d/'; if (fs.existsSync(completionDir)) { fs.copyFileSync(path.join(__dirname,'ttag'), path.join(completionDir,'ttag')) }`. A hardcoded absolute SYSTEM directory — outside the project AND outside the user's home, which is meaningfully more sensitive than a dotfile write. The cheapest refusal in the catalog: the package's own guard already treats a missing or unwritable directory as an expected outcome and just skips the completion with a warning, so nothing the user asked for is lost.
packages.observed: The literal completionDir constant and the guarded copyFileSync, read from the published tarball.

deferred.why: A demonstrated need whose grant SHAPE cannot be written from the evidence in hand. scripts/postinstall.js reads the consumer's package.json (baseline-granted) and, when pkg.egg.typescript or pkg.egg.declarations is set, spawns egg-ts-helper — a SEPARATE package — which writes generated .d.ts files into the consumer project. The source read did not trace egg-ts-helper, so the write target is unknown, and a grant cannot be bounded by a mechanism nobody has read. NOT a refusal: nothing here suggests the write is illegitimate. Next step is reading egg-ts-helper's own source for its output path.

deferred.scope: in-place rewrites of a sibling package's .d.ts files
deferred.why: postinstall.js's findCypressTypes() does require.resolve('cypress/package.json') to locate the consumer's installed cypress SIBLING package, then REWRITES that package's own .d.ts files in place to comment out global declarations. That is the same shape as esoftplay's in-place patching of other packages — the vector the jail exists to close — but the source-read lane left grant_recommended UNSET rather than false, so recording it as a refusal would be this catalog inventing a verdict the data does not carry. Deferred with the concern stated. If the shape holds under review it belongs in `packages` above with reason `patches-other-packages`.

deferred.scope: unknown; likely host or system config directories
deferred.why: The only UNDETERMINED failure mode in the corpus. The preinstall step was traced and is GRACEFUL; the install step's real filesystem footprint was not traced within the lane's budget, and ioBroker's own documented architecture describes first-time PLATFORM setup — host or system config directories rather than project-local files. No grant can be written, and no refusal either.

notNeededRatherThanRefused.why: Carries grant_recommended:false in the source-read data like the nine refusals above, but for the OPPOSITE reason, and it must not be read as one: on the ordinary published-package install path (PERCY_POSTINSTALL_BROWSER unset, no shipped ./src) both branches of postinstall.js evaluate false and the script is a complete no-op — no network, no filesystem writes. Its .local-chromium/ target is inside its own package directory and its storage.googleapis.com fetch happens only behind an explicit opt-in. Nothing is denied because nothing is attempted.

Recorded here to correct a mistake in this effort's own summary, which listed it among the refusals. The source read REFUTED that framing: the consumer's project-root config.xml is READ ONLY (never written — every fs.writeFileSync targets the plugin's own plugin.xml inside its own package dir), and the lane recommended a grant. The read is a single named file and the Cordova convention for finding a <preference> element. It needs no packageGrants entry because a project-root file read is not what the jail denies; it is listed so nobody re-derives the refusal from the earlier summary.

knownDefects.what: `packageNetwork` describes a package-identity gate on egress that nothing enforces. `preset::build_jail_net` compiles to `["$downloads"]` for every jailed lifecycle spawn, so a package with NO catalog entry still reaches all 33 admitted hosts.
knownDefects.why: Egress was global before the catalog recorded per-package need, and the data that makes a per-package gate possible only arrived with v2's corpus. Flipping it is a behavioral change, not a data change: every package the corpus did not name loses network, which is the intended design and needs its own measurement pass.
knownDefects.next: Thread `package_name` into `build_jail_surface` so the net axis emits PackageNetwork::NoEntry as deny-all, a host list as those hosts, and Full as unrestricted. This is what makes the PR-submission contract real rather than aspirational, and it is the highest-value change the catalog now enables.

knownDefects.what: The macOS entry for `@prisma/client` records a 71282 B generated client carrying a per-run schema nonce. On the version the entry names (6.19.3) that artifact cannot be produced at all, on any platform, jailed or not.
knownDefects.why: The postinstall's getLocalPackagePath() calls `require.resolve('prisma')`, which throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on 6.19.3 (its `main` is build/index.js but resolution reaches build/types.js, which is not shipped), so `prisma generate` never runs and the script emits only throw-stubs. Verified directly on Linux with an UNCONFINED baseline. The macOS run must have had a resolvable CLI — an earlier 6.x, a workspace layout, or a global install.
knownDefects.next: Re-run the macOS arm and record which version and layout produced the nonce-bearing client, or downgrade the macOS `observed` to the artifact that actually reproduces. The Linux conclusion is unaffected: it rests on granted being byte-identical to unconfined, which is a stronger control than artifact size.

knownDefects.what: `projectWrites.literal` hits the same absent-path Landlock rule drop that `siblingDirs` did: with `<project>/.git/hooks` absent, the granted arm cannot create it. Measured on Landlock ABI 7 and pinned by a test so it cannot regress silently.
knownDefects.why: Fixed for `siblingDirs` by materializing the directory during compilation, because that path is inside nub's own dependency tree. The same side effect inside a CONSUMER's `.git` is a different call and was deliberately not made here. In practice a real checkout always has `.git/hooks` (git creates it with samples), so the nine hook-installer grants work — `git-commit-msg-linter` is the one that explicitly mkdirs it when missing.
knownDefects.next: Either materialize literal write targets too, scoped to directories the grant already covers, or accept the limitation and say so in the entry. Decide deliberately rather than by discovering it.

knownDefects.what: @danmarshall/deckgl-typings and msw were each measured as a complete no-op even UNJAILED in a later corpus run, which does not square with the EPERM each grant was written against.
knownDefects.why: For msw the two results are consistent — its postinstall is a no-op unless the consumer's manifest declares msw.workerDirectory, which a fixture that does not declare it never exercises. For @danmarshall/deckgl-typings there is no such explanation yet. Neither package is in the 230-package source-read corpus, so v2 adds no evidence.
knownDefects.next: Re-run @danmarshall/deckgl-typings against a fixture that actually installs it as a dependency and check for the 20 copied type folders. Both grants are harmless if the no-op result is right — an unused grant confers nothing on a script that does nothing — so this is a tidiness defect, not a live risk.

knownDefects.what: systemPaths is recorded and code-generated but not folded into build_jail_surface, so the 17 packages it covers still fail.
knownDefects.why: Wiring it changes the granted read set on every platform and interacts with the backends' minimal-root closures. That is a measured change, not a data change, and v2 is the data.
knownDefects.next: Fold compiler::system_read_paths() into the build-jail read set behind a differential on canvas and msnodesqlv8, which between them exercise pkg-config, ldconfig and the widest hardcoded path set in the corpus.

knownDefects.what: Eleven of the fourteen packageGrants and most of the new networkHosts carry evidence:"source-read", not "measured". No install was run to confirm the grant fixes the break.
knownDefects.why: Deliberate, and the reason is in failureModes: 34 of 230 packages fail SILENTLY, so an exit-code-based measurement structurally cannot see the failures that matter most. A measurement-only bar would have left every one of those uncovered. Source-read is the weaker evidence class and the `evidence` field says so on every entry that rests on it.
knownDefects.next: Promote entries to measured opportunistically as the corpus harness gains a work signal that is not the exit code. Do not gate the grants on it — an unexercised grant costs nothing and a missing one breaks an install.

pathShapeNote: `pathShape` on a host entry is PROVENANCE — what the package was observed to fetch — and NOT a gate. Nothing enforces it and nothing should be built to. The reason is the threat model: the defense the build jail actually provides is PACKAGE IDENTITY (a package with no catalog entry gets no egress, and one that needs egress arrives through a pull request), so narrowing an admitted host to a URL prefix would constrain a package somebody already reviewed while doing nothing about the unvetted package a worm just bolted a postinstall onto — which is the actual attack. The data is kept because it cost nothing to gather and it tells a reviewer what an entry was admitted FOR.
